summary: The Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025 revises rules for the National School Lunch Program to allow schools to offer whole and reduced-fat milk, both organic and nonorganic. It removes the requirement that milk must match the most recent Dietary Guidelines for Americans. It also expands allowable nondairy beverage options, allows parents or legal guardians to provide a written statement for milk substitutes for students with dietary-restricting disabilities, excludes fluid milk fat from saturated fat calculations for school meals, and requires school food service personnel to receive annual training and certification on food allergies.

affected_groups.effect: Can be offered whole, reduced-fat, and organic milk options, as well as qualifying nutritionally equivalent nondairy beverages, and have expanded options for milk substitutes backed by parents or legal guardians.
affected_groups.group: Students in the National School Lunch Program

affected_groups.effect: Must receive annual training and certification that includes a specific module on food allergies and best practices for preventing, recognizing, and responding to reactions.

key_provisions: Allows schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer students whole, reduced-fat (2%), low-fat (1%), and fat-free flavored or unflavored milk, which may be organic or nonorganic.
Removes the requirement that school milk must be consistent with the most recent Dietary Guidelines for Americans.
Expands nondairy beverage options to include those nutritionally equivalent to fluid milk that meet USDA standards.
Permits a parent or legal guardian, in addition to a licensed physician, to provide a written statement requesting a fluid milk substitute for a student whose disability restricts their diet.
Excludes fluid milk fat from the saturated fat content calculation for school meals.
Requires local school food service personnel to receive annual training and certification that includes a module on food allergies.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025 revises rules for the National School Lunch Program to allow schools to offer whole and reduced-fat milk, both organic and nonorganic. It removes the requirement that milk must match the most recent Dietary Guidelines for Americans. It also expands allowable nondairy beverage options, allows parents or legal guardians to provide a written statement for milk substitutes for students with dietary-restricting disabilities, excludes fluid milk fat from saturated fat calculations for school meals, and requires school food service personnel to receive annual training and certification on food allergies.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation modifies federal nutrition standards for school meals by expanding the types of milk and beverages schools can offer, changing how saturated fat is calculated for school meals, and mandating food allergy training and certification for food service workers.
